2. "Banglar Bani" used to be printed and published from Dacca as a daily Bengali newspaper by late Sk. Fazlul Huque Moni till 13.6.75, when the declaration and authentication in respect of the said newspaper made under Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973 stood annulled upon the promulgation of Newspapers (Annulment of Declaration) Ordinance No. XXXIII of 1975 on 13th June 1975. Since there is no existence of "Banglar Bani" as a Bengali daily newspaper. Thereafter by Ordinance No. L of 1976 dated 30th June, 1976 the aforesaid Newpapers (Annulment of Declaration) Act, XLII of 1975 was also repealed which afforded a fresh opportunity for printing and publishing of the aforesaid Bengali daily newspaper "Banglar Bani" again. 

 3. Meanwhile late Sk. Fazlul Huque Moni having been killed in the uprising of 15th August, 1975, his younger brother the present petitioner applied to the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca on 23.7.79 to accord permission to print and publish a daily Bengali newspaper under the name and style of "Banglar Bani" and made a declaration in respect thereof for authentication under Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973. This was also accompanied with a certificate issued by a Manager of Uttara Bank on 23.7.79 that the Bani Group of Publications Ltd. the proposed Printer & Publisher of daily Bengali newspaper "Banglar Bani" had a credit balance of Taka 1,00,000 (one lac) in their bank account; this was invariably done to comply with the requirements of clause (g) of sub-section (2) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973 as amended by clause (c) of section 2 of Ordinance III of 1977 by way of an addition of an Explanation thereto. The petitioner was formerly an Assistant Editor of the daily Begali newspaper Banglar Bani and also the printer and publisher of Bangladesh Times prior to the promulgation of Newspapers (Annulment of Declaration) Ordinance No. XXXIII of 1975 on 13th June 1975. 

 5. From the perusal of the application and declaration of the petitioner filed before the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca on 23.7.79 alongwith the. Banker's Certificate, it does not appear anywhere that he has not fulfilled any of the requirements mentioned in clauses (a)(b) of sub-section (2) of section 12 of the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973, in order to obtain an authentication of the declaration made by the petitioner with regard to printing and publication of the proposed Bangali daily newspaper "Banglar Bani". It appears that the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca before whom the petitioner made the declaration for the purpose of printing and publishing "Banglar Bani" did not say anywhere at any time that the petitioner did not fulfill the requirements of clauses (a)-(h) of sub-section (2) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973. The Deputy Commissioner by his impugned memo merely informed the petitioner of the inability of the Government to grant permission to authenticate the declaration in respect of "Banglar Bani". 

 6. In the aforesaid circumstances, it is necessary to fall back upon the relevant provisions of the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973. Section 5 of the Act says that no newspaper shall be printed or published unless there subsists an authenticated declaration in respect thereof. Section 7 of the Act says that the printer and publisher of every newspaper shall appear before the District Magistrate within whose local jurisdiction such newspapers shall be printed and published, and shall make and subscribe a declaration he Form-B of the schedule to the Act. Section 12 of the Act lays down the procedure for authentication of a decoration in respect of a newspaper. Subsection (2) of section 12 of the Act says that the District Magistrate shall not authenticate a declaration unless he is satisfied upon the requirements referred to in clauses (a)-(h) thereof. Sub-section 3 of section 12 of the Act says that if the District Magistrate refuses to authenticate a declaration, the person making the declaration may prefer an appeal to the Government against such refusal. From consideration of the provisions of sections 7 and 12 of Act XXIII of 1973, it clearly appears that the power to authenticate a declaration in respect of a newspaper has been given to the District Magistrate within whose jurisdiction such newspaper is to be printed and published and against any refusal of the District Magistrate to authenticate any declaration, an appeal shall lie to the Government. So far as the District Magistrate is concerned, it has not been defined any where in Act XXIII of 1973 and consequently the only definition thereof made in section 10 of the Code of Criminal Procedure will have to be followed. It can not be disputed that the office of the District Magistrate under section 10 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is primarily a quasi judicial, if not a judicial one. In Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act, XXIII of 1973, the power to authenticate a declaration in respect of a newspaper being given to the District Magistrate under sections 7 and 12 thereof the proceeding by its very nature is a quasi judicial one. Section 7 of Act XXIII of 1973 says that the printer and publisher of every newspaper shall appear before the District Magistrate while making and subscribing the declaration. Sub-section (2) of section 12 of the Act empowers the District Magistrate to authenticate a declaration after being satisfied about the requirements contained in clauses (a)-(h) therein. Sub-section (3) of section 12 further provides for a statutory appeal to the Government against any decision of the District Magistrate refusing to authenticate a declaration. Considering the aforesaid provisions of sections 7 and 12 of Act XXIII of 1973, there is no doubt that the proceeding before the District Magistrate as aforesaid is a quasi judicial one which warrants the District Magistrate to afford a personal hearing to the person making the declaration. In this connection it may be mentioned that sub-section (2) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973 says that the District Magistrate shall not authenticate a declaration unless he is satisfied that the person making the declaration did the requirements contained in clauses (a)-(h) thereof; inevitably means that if a person making a declaration can satisfy the District Magistrate that the requirements contained in clauses (a)-(h) of sub-section (2) of section 12 of the Act have been fulfilled, in such circumstances, the District Magistrate has no other option but to authenticate the declaration as such. 

 7. In the present case it will have to be considered whether the District Magistrate as aforesaid was satisfied as to whether the petitioner fulfilled the requirements contained in clauses (a)-(h) of sub-section (2) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973. Although notice of this Rule was served upon the Ministry of Home Affairs and Deputy Commissioner of Dacca being the respondents herein and although the order of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca has been impugned in this Rule, a Section Officer in the Ministry of Home Affairs has only affirmed and filed an affidavit-in-opposition to this writ petition and no affidavit-in-opposition has been filed on behalf of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca, Consequently this Court had to call for the relevant file of this case lying with the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca and it was produced before the Court by the learned Additional Attorney General appearing for the respondents. From the perusal of the file, notice of the Court was drawn to Memo No. 1279 (enclose)/Eng/X/1/79 dated 17-12-79 addressed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) Dacca to the Section Officer, Ministry of Home Affairs (Political Branch) and also to another Memo No. 8584/62-79/ General dated 21-9-79 addressed from the office of D.I.G. of Police Special Branch to the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca. So far as the memo from the office of the D.I.G. of Police, Special Branch is concerned, it shows that in view of the political background of the petitioner, his application for authentication of the declaration with regard to the printing and publishing of "Banglar Bani" could not be recommended. Considering such opinion of the D.I.G. of Police, Special Branch, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) Dacca exercising the functions of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca in his memo to the Ministry of Home Affairs as aforesaid observed as follows:- 

 8. It is thus clear from the aforesaid observation made on behalf of the Deputy Court missioner of Dacca in the memo addressed to the Ministry of Home Affairs that the Deputy. Commissioner acting as a District Magistrate was not only satisfied that the petitioner had fulfilled all the requirements mentioned in clauses (a)-(h) of sub-section (2) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973 but also recommended to the Ministry of Home Affairs for authentication of the petitioner's declaration made in respect of printing and publishing of "Banglar Bani". As has been already observed hereinbefore that once the District Magistrate is satisfied that the person making the declaration fulfilled all the requirements mentioned in clauses a-h of sub-section 2 of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973, the District Magistrate has no option but to authenticate the declaration as such. In the present case, the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca acting as a District Magistrate having been satisfied about the petitioner's declaration ought to have authenticated such declaration by himself without further referring the matter to the Ministry of Home Affairs. When under sub-sections (3) and (4) of section 12 of XXIII of 1973 them is a provision for statutory appeal and application to the Government against any refusal or inability of any District Magistrate to authenticate any declaration, the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca, in the present case, could not refer the matter to the Ministry of Home Affairs as such. From the reading of the impugned memo of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca it appears that the Deputy Commissioner acting as the District Magistrate did not signify his refusal or inability to authenticate the declaration, but merely informed the petitioner of the inability of the Government to authenticate the petitioner's declaration with regard to the printing and publication of "Banglar Bani." By the impugned memo the authority of the District Magistrate has been subrogated by the Government, by juxtaposition, of the provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973. By such action not only that the petitioner has been deprived from preferring an appeal to the Government but the Deputy Commissioner acting as a District Magistrate exercising a quasi judicial function refused to authenticate the declaration of the petitioner upon an instruction from its appellate authority without applying the principle and rule of natural justice by affording the petitioner with a personal hearing in this matter. The impugned memo of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca must, on that account, be held to have been made illegally, without any lawful authority and with no legal effect. 

 9. In this connection it may be mentioned that after the lifting of Martial Law and the restoration of the Constitution and after the lifting of Emergency and restoration of Fundamental Rights, at present Article 39 of the Constitution is very much operative. Under clause (b) of Sub-Article (2) of Article 39 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, freedom of the Press is guaranteed, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, or in relation to contempt of court, defamation or incitement to an offence. The aforesaid qualifying provisions to the citizens' freedom of the Press guaranteed in the Constitution can only arise after a particular newspaper is allowed to be printed and published upon the authentication of a declaration made under sections 7 and 12 of the Printing Press and Publication (Declaration and Registration) Act XXIII of 1973. In view of the aforesaid Constitutional right of the citizens of Bangladesh guaranteeing freedom of the Press under clause (b) of sub-article (2) of Article 39 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, the opinion of the D.I.G. of Police that the Petitioner's declaration could not be authenticated in view of his political background as mentioned hereinbefore must be held to be illegal and unconstitutional. In this connection reference may be made to a Full Bench decision of East Pakistan High Court reported in (1967) 19 DLR (Dec.) 581—PLD 1969 (Dacca) 463 in the matter of Sangbad Ltd. and also to another Division Bench Decision of the West Pakistan High Court reported in PLD 1962 (W.P. Karachi) 537. 

 10. Be that as it may, when it clearly appears from the memo of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca addressed to the Ministry of Home Affairs as aforesaid that the Deputy Commissioner acting as the District Magistrate was satisfied that the Petitioner's declaration with regard to the printing and publication of "Banglar Bani" should be authenticated and the Deputy Commissioner could not do so in view of the inability of the Government to grant such authentication of the declaration, the Government being as appellate authority under sub-sections (3) and (4) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973, refusal or inability of the Deputy Commissioner's declaration was made under the direct instruction of the Government. In such circumstances, the impugned memo of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca was made by virtue of a colorable exercise of authority vested in him under sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 12 of Act XXIII of 1973. On that account the impugned memo No. 567/Eng/X/1/80 dated 19.5.80 issued from the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Dacca having already been held to have been made illegally, without any lawful authority and with no legal effect must be set aside. The Deputy Commissioner of Dacca acting as a District Magistrate and the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs of the Government of Bangladesh being respondents herein are directed to authenticate the declaration of the petitioner as Printer and Publisher of the Bengali daily newspaper under the name and style of "Banglar Bani" forthwith.
